messages.subject: D-RUG work group Wed: 10-12
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This is your reminder that the highly anticipated and frequently celebrated meeting of the Davis R Users’ Group is meeting again tomorrow 10-12. Meetings this quarter are in hybrid format, both on zoom and in-person at the DataLab classroom. Details are below.

See you tomorrow!

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators – Christine, Christian, Liza, Martha, Ryan, and Wesley

_______________________________________________________________
This Winter quarter we'll be meeting from 10-12 on Wednesdays in a hybrid format, via zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>, and in the Data Lab classroom (360 Shields Library).

Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar <https://d-rug.github.io/calendar.html>! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).
_______________________________________________________________

--
Christine Parisek, MS
PhD Candidate | Ecology Graduate Group
Department of Wildlife, Fish, & Conservation Biology
University of California, Davis
caparisek.github.io <http://caparisek.github.io>

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Davis R Users' Group - Wednesday 10am-12pm
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

Special update! Tomorrow at 10am you will also have the opportunity to hear a short 20min presentation from one of your very own D-RUG Coordinators, Wesley Brooks.

Title: Do e-bikes reduce car use? Design, simulation, and power analysis for a study of e-bike use in Sacramento

Abstract: Micromobility services like subscription e-bikes and e-scooters offer people new modes of travel in urban environments. Meanwhile, minimizing car travel is important for limiting the negative effects of air pollution and CO2 emissions. Thus, micromobility services would be an environmental boon if people use them instead of driving - but it is currently unknown whether that substitution is happening. In this talk, Dr. Wesley Brooks will describe the design and analysis of a study that aims to measure the substitution of vehicle use with micromobility services. The statistical power of several candidate designs is simulated using a hierarchical Bayesian model based on integrating data from multiple sources and scales.

Happy coding,
Christine

--
Christine Parisek, MS
PhD Candidate | Ecology Graduate Group
Department of Wildlife, Fish, & Conservation Biology
University of California, Davis
caparisek.github.io <http://caparisek.github.io>
